label: <DEL> step in long sequences starting with 1 or n
explanation: Very sparse feature (about 0.08% of sequences) that fires only at the delimiter step (t == L, mass share 1.0), never in the original or copy phases. Activation depends mostly on the first original token, which is also the first output: 1 (64% of mass) or n (26%), with small amounts for y/f/x. It favors longer sequences (L 7-8 peak, none for L <= 4). Larger values come with a last original token (prev_tok) of v, d, m or w, and a second token from {1, y, z, x, n}. Top examples look like 1 1 z z 1 d <DEL> and 1 y z m v <DEL>. The simple predicate covers about 87% of activation mass but has very low precision (about 1.5%), because most delimiter steps with first token 1/n do not fire. A conjunction that also requires the second token and last token reaches only F1 of about 0.29, so the full gating condition is a sparse, uncaptured combination of the first, second and last tokens.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=1 & out_tok=1 (+5.37), phase=1 & out_tok=n (+4.21), prev_tok=v (+3.57), orig2=z (+3.19), prev_tok=d (+2.66), phase=1 & out_tok=y (+2.36). Lower it: in_first=0 (-2.91), in_count=1 (-1.77), orig5=- (-1.40), to_go=3 (-1.37).
